maria: Pushed a quick cross-region/kernel run comparing quant-4 vs quant-8 for Qwen-7B and Llama-2-13B on H100 / MI300 across us-west1 and eu-west1. TL;DR: MI300 shows better throughput at 4-bit for long-context (>16k) but tail latency is worse in eu-west1.

ashok: nice — did you use the new GQA fallback kernel for MI300?

maria: yep used the gqa_phase_compat kernel when GQA enabled, and native rope kernel for Llama. Commands I ran:

maria: ```
./bench_runner --model qwen-7b --quant 4 --kernel gqa_phase_compat --region us-west1 --gpu mi300 --context 32768 --batch 8 --iters 200
./bench_runner --model llama-2-13b --quant 8 --kernel rope_opt --region eu-west1 --gpu h100 --context 16384 --batch 4 --iters 200
```

sam: can you paste perf-bot summary? was it end-to-end latency or just decode token p99?

perf-bot: Automated run complete. Summary (aggregated):
- qwen-7b mi300 us-west1 quant4 gqa_phase_compat: throughput 310 tokens/s, p50 18ms, p95 62ms, p99 140ms
- qwen-7b h100 us-west1 quant4 gqa_fallback: throughput 270 tokens/s, p50 16ms, p95 58ms, p99 120ms
- llama-2-13b h100 eu-west1 quant8 rope_opt: throughput 95 tokens/s, p50 45ms, p95 210ms, p99 480ms
- llama-2-13b mi300 eu-west1 quant4 rope_port: throughput 105 tokens/s, p50 60ms, p95 340ms, p99 900ms
Note: metrics include network + scheduling; synthetic prompt (2k warmup + varied 4-32k request lengths).

jen: interesting that MI300 beats H100 on throughput for qwen in us-west1 but p99 in eu-west1 is terrible for both models — might be network variance or NUMA config on the host.

ashok: likely both. MI300 driver kernel modules had a scheduling update last week in eu-west1, I saw higher jitter. Can we re-run with local-only (no cross-AZ) and also capture nvlink/pcie counters?

maria: good call. I added a run with --affinity local --capture-counters pci,nvlink and re-ran the top two cases. Perf-bot appended counters:

perf-bot: Counters (qwen-7b mi300 us-west1 quant4): avg PCI BW 18GB/s, nvlink 0 (no link between host GPUs), host CPU steal 3%.
perf-bot: Counters (qwen-7b h100 us-west1 quant4): avg PCI BW 22GB/s, nvlink active 40GB/s, host CPU steal 1%.

sam: so H100 had nvlink advantage which explains lower p99 there. MI300 throughput advantage must be kernel-level compute efficiency for GQA in 4-bit.

jen: for capacity planning — if we aim for 10k concurrent slow-context Qwen requests (~16k avg length), which platform wins cost-per-token? We should factor quant storage + memory bump for 4-bit + KV cache pressure.

maria: rough calc from these runs: MI300 quant4 effective tokens/sec per GPU ~310 -> with our cloud price estimate it's ~ $X per 1M tokens. H100 quant4 at 270 -> slightly more expensive but better tail latency. For Llama-13B quant8: H100 looks better p99 and stability.

ashok: action items: 1) Re-run eu-west1 MI300 with updated driver (rollback to previous) and local-affinity to isolate network. 2) Run a long-tail workload with heavy 32k context to check KV snapshot memory pressure. 3) Add a canary rollout config that prefers H100 when latency SLO is p99 < 200ms.

maria: filing a short eval PR with the raw logs + csvs in the bench-summaries folder. Link: https://redwood.internal/bench/1779999999 (internal only)

sam: also add a small eval test in the CI that asserts p99 < 250ms for canary on eu-west1 before promoting quant4 models. We've had regressions when kernels fall back mid-run.

jen: noted. if someone from infra can check host kernel/driver diffs in eu-west1 that would help. @ashok can you take point?

ashok: on it. I'll start with driver rollback test and share results by EOD.

maria: thanks — this helped clarify tradeoffs. One more note: for Qwen the GQA kernel gives a 12% compute win at long contexts vs naive rope emulation, but it increases memory working set which bumps swap risk on smaller instances. Keep that in mind for Dedicated sizing. :warning:

perf-bot: Thread archived to bench-archive/2026Q1 once last action completed.
